hero.tagline: 24 hours. One weekend. Build something that actually helps people.
hero.location: Concordia University, Downtown Campus, Montréal, Quebec
hero.notifyHeading: Be the first to know when registration opens

vision.paragraph1: Before we started MuslimHacks, we saw a clear problem in Quebec: plenty of talented Muslims in tech, but not enough of a connected network. Our mission is to build that over the next few years, starting by connecting students to Muslim businesses and professionals.
vision.paragraph2: We want people to realize there is a whole Muslim industry out there, and that we do not always need to rely on non-Muslim networks to grow. That is the idea we want to foster, in shaa Allah.
vision.differenceParagraph1: Other Muslim hackathons often started inside ecosystems that were already built for them. Their goal was usually to bring more Muslims into networks that were already flourishing, by the mercy of Allah.
vision.differenceParagraph2: Quebec is not the same. We are building from scratch and trying to lay the foundations of the network we envision here, in shaa Allah. One weekend will not solve everything, but we hope MuslimHacks becomes a stepping stone toward that goal.

benefits.titlePrefix: It's free, and you leave with
benefits.intro: There is no fee to attend. Everything on this list is part of the weekend.

items.title: Free food
items.body: Every meal is covered while you're here. Just show up and build.

items.title: Mentorship from Muslim professionals
items.body: Industry mentors sit with you during the build and help you get unstuck.

items.title: Networking with Muslim businesses
items.body: Meet founders and companies from the Muslim industry we're building here in Quebec.

items.title: Internship opportunities
items.body: Recruiters will be at the event in shaa Allah, so your project can turn into a job lead.

items.title: Investment in your project
items.body: If investors believe in what you built, the weekend doesn't have to be where it ends.

question.titlePrefix: What if your code could be
question.hadithQuote: "The best of people are those most beneficial to others."
question.body: Most of us already write code for school or work. MuslimHacks is about putting that same energy toward something that helps people, with a real intention behind it.

people.title: Show up together
people.body: Muslims and friends of the community, designers, organizers, and people still learning to code. If you care about the work, you belong here.

work.title: Solve real problems
work.body: You've got 24 hours. Pick something that actually affects Muslim communities, like access to resources, education, or local needs, and try to ship something useful.

point.title: Leave something behind
point.body: We're hoping some of these projects keep going after the weekend. Open-source tools, charity platforms, small apps people can keep using.

values.pastWeekendsCaption: Late nights, sticky notes, and people who stayed to help.

photoAlts.collaborating: Group collaborating on laptops at a hackathon
photoAlts.pairProgramming: Pair programming at a community event

sponsors.intro: Sponsoring MuslimHacks supports students building for their communities, and funds raised go to charity through Islamic Relief Canada.
sponsors.partnerCtaBody: You'll reach Muslim students and builders across Quebec, plus people who care about the communities we serve.

items.question: Do I need to be Muslim to participate?
items.answer: Nope. The event is rooted in Islamic values of service and charity, but anyone who wants to build something useful is welcome.

items.question: Do I need a team?
items.answer: You can come solo or with up to 4 people. If you show up alone, we'll help you find a team on the first evening.

items.question: Will you offer travel reimbursements?
items.answer: Not this year, unfortunately. We know travel can be tough, and we hope to support it more as the event grows.

items.question: Is the event in-person or virtual?
items.answer: In person, in Quebec. We want people in the same room, not just on a Zoom call.

items.question: What's the cost?
items.answer: It's free. We still fundraise for charity through Islamic Relief Canada.

items.question: Will there be prayer spaces and halal food?
items.answer: Yes. We'll have prayer space, and there's a masjid nearby. All food is halal, and we can work with dietary restrictions.

items.question: What if I'm a beginner?
items.answer: You're good. Bring what you know. There will be mentors and workshops, and plenty of people still figuring things out too.

items.question: How are projects judged?
items.answer: We look at impact, how well it's built, creativity, and the pitch. Mostly though: does this actually help someone?
